title: Member Handbook — Taking Part in Care Management Is Your Choice
content:
Care Management at Prairie Ridge Health Plan is voluntary. Your care management episode becomes active only on your own consent, and only you or your authorized representative can give that consent.

## Your consent

- The episode is activated only when the member or the authorized representative on file states consent during the contact.
- The consent that counts is the statement made by you, or by the authorized representative on file for you, during the contact itself. Nobody else — a relative who is not your authorized representative on file, a provider, or a care team member — can give it for you.
- The date you consent is the date your participation begins; your episode moves from outreach to active on that date.

## If you decline

A member who declines is closed with the closure reason member declined, and may self-refer again after the tier's re-enrollment wait, counted in calendar days after that closure.

## Who may consent (hypothetical callers)

| Person stating consent during the contact | Episode activated on that statement |
|---|---|
| The member | Yes |
| The member's authorized representative on file | Yes |
| The member's adult child, not on file as authorized representative | No |
| The member's primary care provider | No |

## Questions answered

**Can my daughter agree for me?** Only if she is your authorized representative on file. Otherwise the episode is not activated on her statement.

**Is my consent something the care team looks up?** No. Consent is what you, or your authorized representative on file, say during the contact.

**I said no last month. Can I come back?** Yes. A member who declined may self-refer again after the re-enrollment wait for the tier, which runs in calendar days after the closure for the reason member declined.
